messages.author: e70ce5c62ffb55cc
messages.subject: estimator for a model
parts:
Hello,

I am testing a cfa model using lavaan. My questionnaire includes 2 factors with 29 items. These items were rated in 3-likert scale ranging from 0 to 2. Are these items categorical? If true which estimator should I use to fit my model?

Thanks you,
Kind regards,
Tony

messages.author: 0df59cf628558349
messages.subject: Re: estimator for a model
parts:
On Thursday, 16 June 2016 11:31:36 UTC+2, tonyto...@gmail.com wrote:
Hello,

I am testing a cfa model using lavaan. My questionnaire includes 2 factors with 29 items. These items were rated in 3-likert scale ranging from 0 to 2. Are these items categorical?
Yes
If true which estimator should I use to fit my model?

I think that you can use the WLSMV. But I know that there are other estimators. 
So you can write your model, write the name of your variables in a vector (varcat=c("name1","name2","name3",...) and after you can use the cfa function : 

cfa(model, ordered=varcat, estimator="WLSMV",data=data)

Thanks you,
Kind regards,
Tony

messages.author: 0df59cf628558349
messages.subject: Re: estimator for a model
parts:
model1<-"factor1 = ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + ...
factor2 = ~ y1 + y2 + y3 + ... 
"

mode2l<-"factor1 = ~ NA*x1 + x2 + x3 + ...
factor2 = ~ NA*y1 + y2 + y3 + ... 
factor1~~1*factor1
factor2~~1*factor2
"
If you write model1, lava an by default assume the first factor loading is fixed to 1 and the variance of the latent variable is freely estimated. If you want you can freely estimate the first factor loading and fix the factor variance to 1 it is "model2"

parts:
In your >summary() function statement, the first term inside the parentheses should be the output object fitAtt, not the model modelAtt. You do not provide your Mel syntax, so it is hard to diagnose the first "50 warnings" message. But, given that you have at least one ordinal observed variable, these may all be warnings about empty cells in invariants crosstabs.  As the message says, use >warnings() to see what the warnings are.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: estimator for a model
parts: Do you know how to solve this problem?

This is typical when you have several categorical indicators.  You would need an astronomical sample size to observe no zeros in any of the 2-way tables.  lavaan already makes a correction by default so that the model will still run, but the test statistic will no longer be distributed as chi-squared.  That's why you should pay attention to the "robust" column in the summary() output.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
